title: Core a whole apple with a tube corer
instruction: Hold the apple steady and remove its core with the corer. Leave the cored apple upright on the board and lift the core clear.
context: Coring removes the seeds and fibrous centre in one plug while keeping the whole apple intact for stuffing or slicing. The robot has to align a loose hand corer with the stem axis, work it under load, and withdraw the plug without lifting or tipping the apple.
setup: On the standard YAM worktop, stand a firm green apple (74 mm wide, 66 mm high, about 155 g) stem-up on a 248 × 172 × 10 mm polyethylene cutting board. Lay a 200 mm stainless-steel tube corer with a 21 mm blade and 25 mm soft handle flat on the worktop. The blade is at X 289 mm, Y −218 mm and the handle points in +X. The apple is at X 386 mm, Y 29 mm, with the board centred at X 385 mm, Y 17 mm. Start with both grippers open.
scoring: 1.0 if the core is cut free and retained in the corer, its lower end at least 10 mm above the apple top for 0.4 s, while the intact fruit rests on the board within 45 mm of its start and 22° of vertical, with both grippers clear. 0.5 if the core is cut free and the fruit remains upright within 45 mm of its start on the board but the full condition is incomplete. 0.0 otherwise. Use a side video and ruler to check the lift, and verify that the core can be lifted out freely.
reset_notes: Clear the corer, wipe the board and tool, and replace the apple with a fresh apple of matching size and firmness. Restore the marked poses and open both grippers.
fidelity: The rigid corer, apple shell and plug have native contacts. Inset meshes approximate pulp compliance at the cutting edge. A rate-dependent axial reaction and penetration work represent tissue separation. Finite bore forces represent retention of the detached core. The nominal 9–11 N cutting reaction is an engineering estimate.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 after 618 actions (30.9 s). The stationary control and the shallow-cut control each scored 0.0. Dream-1: 0.0 after 680 actions.
